llm.summary: The skill fits patent comparison, but weak handling of account keys warrants review.

dimensions.detail: patentmax_client.py accepts an unrestricted PATENTMAX_BASE_URL and attaches the bearer key without enforcing HTTPS or an approved origin. A local synthetic-token check confirmed that its default redirect mechanism retains Authorization across hosts and HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled Python client uses standard-library modules. No dependency installation, remote code execution, or privileged installer appears.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main workflow covers two or three patents, discloses fees, and provides spending controls. Chinese output and a one-time service promotion are explicit.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The trial-expiry flow asks users to send a live key through chat and directs the agent to save plaintext in ~/.patentmax/api_key.txt for automatic reuse across PatentMax skills. Unlike trial-key storage, this instruction requires no restrictive file permissions. Normal setup documentation primarily describes environment variables.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes claim decomposition, comparison, and CSV delivery. Broader patent-search helpers are explicitly documented as shared supporting tools.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before supplying a paid key, ask the publisher to enforce HTTPS and block credential-bearing redirects to other hosts. Prefer a dedicated low-limit key supplied through the environment, avoid pasting it into chat, review any saved api_key.txt, and approve confidential technical details before external searches.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The trial-registration request sends only a fixed source label, not credentials or arbitrary environment contents. The claimed credential exfiltration at this call is unsupported.
[TT3] unexpected: PatentMax authentication is expected, but unrestricted credential destinations and credential-preserving redirects are verified weaknesses. They establish exposure risk, not evidence that an actual leak occurred.
[TP4] expected: The complete skill implements comparison through agent instructions and Write-based CSV creation. Shared research commands and example company searches are documented, not automatic unrelated actions. The diagnostic prints only the standard eight-character key prefix.
[LP1] expected: Environment access and networking support the disclosed authenticated API client. Bash is declared; the artifacts do not establish a runtime permission bypass.
[E1] expected: The cited URLs belong to the disclosed PatentMax integration or its account pages. External API access alone does not demonstrate exfiltration; credential destination controls remain a separate concern.
[SQP-2] expected: The package includes a confidentiality preflight in references/tools.md that explicitly says technical details go to the server. The main comparison requests transmit patent numbers; no automatic upload of an unpublished draft appears.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese conclusions and verbatim Chinese errors are disclosed language choices, without a demonstrated security impact.
